relationship_scope.claim: Braids a local imperial narrative with the history of governing concepts and practices
relationship_scope.evidence: The 2012 interview at 2–3 explains how Fort William and the Black Hole story connect with selectively traced political economy, law and techniques of imperial power. Chatterjee explicitly notes that selection was necessary; no exhaustive global history is inferred.

relationship_scope.claim: Brings popular cultural practices into the historical analysis of imperial power
relationship_scope.evidence: At 2, Chatterjee says he learned through Subaltern Studies to interrogate popular culture theoretically. Theatre and football enter alongside policy and elite discourse. His sweeping claim about what other intellectual historians omit is not adopted.
